messages:
deploy-bot: starting deployment: release/2025.03.12 -> production. toggles: llmroute_v3=enable (canary pinned). pinned-version: v3.2.1. window: 02:00-04:00 UTC. tagging @sasha @morgan for flag ramp plan.

morgan: ack. I'll coordinate the canary cohort. planned ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%. holdpoints at each step, health gates = error_rate < 0.5% && 95p_latency < 300ms.

sasha: sounds good. prefer 10m soak at 1%, 20m at 5%, 15m at 20% (since traffic shape is light overnight). if telemetry looks noisy we should pause and pin back to v3.2.0.

jay: release notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/relnotes/2025-03-12-llmroute-v3. link has rollout matrix and KVs to watch. Also pinning config in deploy manifest: `flag_config: llmroute_v3@v3.2.1`

priya: put a hard rollback trigger: if user-facing error-rate > 1% for 5m OR latency regression > 100ms for 10m then auto-notify and manual rollback recommended. can we make deploy-bot post the rollback command?

ops-oncall: will watch infra. set alert on p95 latency, 5xx rate, and model OOMs. Ops runbook: `rollback -> flip llmroute_v3=false && pin service to v3.2.0`

morgan: deploy-bot, please start canary and tag the flag as `canary: morgan-20250312`. also run the deploy in dry-run health-check first.

deploy-bot: Canary start accepted by pipeline. commands run: `build -> deploy -> flag-toggle canary`. logs: 
```
[2025-03-12T02:07:00Z] build ok
[2025-03-12T02:08:12Z] deploy to canary pool (hosts: 10) started
[2025-03-12T02:10:00Z] flag llmroute_v3 set to 1% (cohort: canary)
```

morgan: canary up. running 10m soak. tagging monitors: @ops-oncall @sasha

sasha: quick sanity check: sample traces look good, small increase in token generation latency ~+18ms p95, within gate. no errors seen in sampling logs.

jay: confirm observability dashboards updated (route/slo/llmroute_v3). rolling to 5% after 10m if no gate hits.

[10 minutes later]
morgan: seeing a small burst in CPU on one host and p95 went +42ms for ~3m, error rate still <0.2%. holding before shift to 5%.

sasha: agree hold. can we run a quick `kvcache` flush on that host and re-evaluate? might be cache pressure.

ops-oncall: flushed KV cache on host host-12, CPU settled. continuing to monitor. if latency stays > +30ms for 10m we should revert.

morgan: ok holding at 1% for another 15m. will update here.

priya: thanks — remind me to add a note in release notes about the ephemeral latency bump and mitigation steps.

deploy-bot: canary heartbeat: healthy=9/10 hosts, error_rate=0.14%, p95_latency=268ms. next step: wait (manual)=true.

morgan: leaving manual hold. will promote to 5% after another 15m if steady.

sasha: small reminder: document in PR the exact rollout durations and the pin-back command used in rollback. saves time if we need to scrap. :thumbsup:

[end thread]
